news.title: Uefa calls emergency meeting as opposition to Fifa plan hardens
news.lede: 55 members to meet on Thursday to coordinate response. ‘Uefa knows there is significant and growing opposition’. Uefa has called an emergency ­meeting of its 55 members for Thursday afternoon to discuss a coordinated response to Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors. A European boycott of Fifa tournaments is among the options under consideration.

news.title: "Possibility of World Cup Boycott" Global Football Community Reacts Strongly to FIFA's Surprise Plan to Establish a Subsidiary
news.lede: The global football community is strongly opposing FIFA's attempt to establish a subsidiary responsible for operating international football tournaments such as the World Cup and to sell part of the subsidiary's shares to private entities. FIFA has even sent an essentially coercive message stating that there will be a huge difference in support funds between member national associations that support their plans and those that do not, raising the possibility of a boycott of next year's Women's World Cup centered around the Union of European Football Associations (UEFA). According to The Athletic and dpa news agency on the 29th (Korean time), FIFA President Gianni Infantino announced plans to establish a subsidiary called "FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE)" to manage operations of international tournaments such as the World Cup, broadcasting rights, and sponsorships.

news.title: FIFA charges Argentina after World Cup final brawl with Spain
news.lede: Sepp Blatter, FIFA chief for 17 years until 2015, has blasted new proposal that moves ‘people’s game’ further from fans. FIFA’s president lobbies for latest, and heavily criticised, proposal for investment in football’s governing body. Americas governing body ‘deeply concerned’ by lack of due process in FIFA private investment plan, AFC ‘disappointed’. How the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise has provoked criticism, including from UEFA and Britain’s new Prime Minister.

news.title: FIFA open investigation itnp Argentina FA over Falklands banner & World Cup final scrap
news.lede: Argentina managed to reach the World Cup final before ultimately losing 1-0 to Spain without having a single shot on target across the 120 minutes. Their campaign wasn’t without controversy though, and football’s governing body have now confirmed they are investigating Argentina. FIFA have opened proceeding against Leandro Paredes for three counts of assault, Nahuel Molina for two counts of the same offence, and Argentina coach Roberto Ayala for one count. Molina is also being investigated for one count of unsporting behaviour, while team-mate Thiago Almada and Spain midfielder Gavi face the same charge.

news.title: Fifa opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina over Falklands banner and final chaos
news.lede: Players held banner after semi-final against England. Paredes and Molina investigated over brawl after final. Fifa has opened disciplinary ­proceedings against Argentina over the Falkland Islands banner ­displayed after their World Cup semi‑final win against England in Atlanta. As Argentina celebrated ­reaching the final with their dramatic 2-1 ­victory, several players held a sign ­proclaiming “Las Malvinas son ­Argentinas” – the ­Malvinas are Argentinian – in ­reference to the ­British overseas territory in the south Atlantic.

news.title: Former FIFA President Blatter Attacks Infantino’s World Cup Plan
news.lede: Meknes - Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter has strongly criticized plans to create a $20 billion subsidiary for the World Cup, insisting that international football's flagship tournament is a global community asset rather than a private corporate vehicle. The ex-FIFA chief, who led the organization for 17 years until 2015, has warned that current president Gianni Infantino’s latest financial proposal pushes the commercialization of global football too far. The 90-year-old voiced sharp concern over the sport's shifting priorities, pointing out that global tournaments should serve fans rather than corporate interests. "Football belongs to no individual and to no institution.
